Former Synagogue in Merchingen (Ravenstein)

Former Synagogue · Ravenstein, Germany

The synagogue in Merchingen was established in its current building on the Buchenweg in the mid-19th century, serving a Jewish community documented in the town since 1737. Its interior was destroyed during the November 1938 pogrom, though the structure survived. The municipality of Merchingen purchased the building in 1940 and used it temporarily as a gymnasium before selling it in 1950 to the Catholic parish of Hüngheim, which converted it into a branch church, adding a bell tower. During renovations in the 1970s, remnants of a genizah containing religious texts and ritual objects were discovered in the roof space. A memorial stone unveiled in 1983 recalls the building's origin as a synagogue.
